intention: ONE PREDICATE over a declared constraint set: something that was constraining the system stopped constraining it, and no ruling sits in the same act. That single comparison covers a `why` that moved, a check that was disabled, a falsifier that was weakened, a threshold that was loosened, and a deterministic red that was suppressed. A ruling cited in the same commit (or landing in it) makes the weakening accountable and the check silent; its absence is the finding. This is the physics behind the prose rule Akien offered and CC accepted the same day, which lands in cairn/CLAUDE.md's 'Rules awaiting physics' in the same act and is a tracked debt from the moment it is written (Law 4). NOTE: this ticket covers face 1 of corrosion (constraint drift). Face 2 (work claimed done but incomplete) is a separate mechanism with a separate detector. The PRIMARY corrosion discriminator is friction (core principles), not provenance — provenance is the accountability axis. See ruling 2026-08-20-corrosion-is-friction-increase-and-optimization-candidates.
why:
AKIEN'S REASON, and it is a claim about CC's behaviour rather than about artifacts: 'presenting a deterministic result of an error will prompt you to fix it, not to plaster over it.' An LLM's opinion that something looks wrong invites negotiation, hedging, and a paragraph explaining why it is acceptable. A deterministic red offers nothing to negotiate with, so the only available move is repair.

But a rule with no exit produces its own defect. Sometimes the check IS wrong, and when the only two moves are plaster or paralysis, CC's measured reflex is plaster. So the rule Akien offered is framed as an ESCAPE ROUTE, verbatim: 'we can add a rule about not plastering over deterministic feedback without a ruling by me if you want. that gives you an escape route.' Requiring a ruling is what makes 'this check is wrong' a sayable thing rather than something smuggled into a rationalising paragraph.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a check goes red; CC writes three paragraphs explaining why this instance is different, environmental, pre-existing, or out of scope; the red is dispositioned into prose and the corpus keeps its green. Nobody is lied to and nothing is recorded as having changed, and the system has quietly lost a constraint. Law 9 already forbids the vocabulary of that move ('there is no triage authority — not environmental, not pre-existing, not out of scope'), which is prose, which is why this ticket exists.

WHY ONE PREDICATE AND NOT FOUR: the unification came from noticing that this rule is the corrosion discriminator one level up. Drift with a ruling behind it is the system learning; drift with no ruling is corrosion. Suppression with a ruling behind it is a corrected check; suppression with no ruling is plaster. Same discriminator, different object — so four checks would have been four implementations of one comparison, kept in step by hand.

gates: PROVE GATE — the tester runs proofs with these teeth: a weakening with no cited ruling REDS; the same weakening with a ruling cited GREENS (the beneficial-drift tooth, the one a hollow build omits); a strengthening is untouched; a narrowing of the constraint set REDS via self-reference; each of the four constraint kinds is exercised by the SAME predicate; a stale unrelated ruling in decisions/ does NOT satisfy the citation. BUILD GATE — build_inspector at the PROVEME crossing. DURABILITY GATE — committed to both repos. KICKS BACK ON — red routes to build at the point of creation (CP2); a firing that turns out to be ordinary mid-build sharpening routes to the SCOPING question and NEVER to disabling the check — written here so it cannot be improvised under pressure.
falsifier: RED if: (1) a constraint is weakened with no ruling cited and the check does not fire; (2) the check fires on a weakening that DOES cite a ruling — a ruled change is the system learning, and redding it is the freeze this design exists to avoid; (3) the constraint set is narrowed and the check does not fire on ITSELF; (4) the check is built to read only `why` fields, when the predicate is general and the why is one member; (5) 'a ruling in the same act' is implemented loosely enough that a pre-existing unrelated ruling satisfies it; (6) the check fires so often on ordinary mid-build sharpening that its output stops being read — measured as more than a third of firings dispositioned 'not really a weakening' over the first 30.

dependencies: The constraint set is a declared, versioned artifact and NOT a regex inside the checker — measured reasoning: the predicate is only as good as the set it watches, and that set is exactly where this check can be quietly hollowed out.

'A ruling in the same act' is defined here and must not loosen: a ruling packet in CairnCommons/decisions/ whose id is cited in the commit that weakened the constraint, or which lands in the same commit. Anything looser reintroduces the negotiation this check removes.
OPEN AND AKIEN'S: are his own commits subject to this? Built to watch CC's, with his flagged as his call.
distinctions_recorded: THIS CHECK MUST BE IN ITS OWN CONSTRAINT SET. It is a check about suppressing checks — the highest-value thing in the corpus to weaken — and it can be killed by the exact move it catches: narrow what it watches and it goes green forever while watching nothing. The self-reference is deliberate and is the difference between a real instrument and a comfortable one.

THE ESCAPE ROUTE IS THE POINT, NOT A LOOPHOLE. A check that made weakening impossible rather than accountable would be a worse artifact than none — it would freeze the corpus, and a learning system must be capable of beneficial drift (Akien, same exchange).

NOT A NEW LAW, and the decision is recorded because choosing not to reify leaves no trace otherwise. This is conduct under Laws 3 and 4, not a new dependency-ordered contract, and Law numbers are ADDRESSES (CLAUDE.md's own note on why Law 10 is numbered last), so inserting one is never free.

AGAINST LAW 6, which is the near neighbour: Law 6 gates WHO may write. This checks whether a write that WAS permitted removed a constraint without a recorded decision. An owner may legitimately weaken their own check; this does not stop them, it requires them to say so. Complementary, not competing.

KNOWN UNKNOWN, STATED AT CAST RATHER THAN DISCOVERED AT BUILD: the false-positive rate. Falsifiers get sharpened mid-build constantly and nobody rules on each edit. Probable scoping is constraints on PROVED nodes only, since a node still building is still being designed. If the check becomes noise it gets ignored — which is corrosion of the corrosion detector.

watchme.trigger: the check has been live for 30 or more commits touching constraint-bearing artifacts and has never once fired — the never-redded signal this corrosion program runs on, turned on the corrosion detector itself, because a check about suppression that never fires is either guarding a clean corpus or watching an empty set and cannot tell you which
watchme.enough: cleared when the check has fired at least once on a real weakening AND at least one firing was dispositioned as a genuine catch rather than noise — an existence claim, because one true catch proves the predicate grips while a count of firings proves only that it is sensitive
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying every firing with its disposition (genuine catch / ordinary sharpening / false positive) and the size of the constraint set at each firing — the set size rides along because a shrinking set is how this instrument dies quietly
